name: Anti-Grain Geometry (AGG 2.6)
workload: Blend2D-style bl_bench suite: filled and stroked rects, rounded rects, triangles, polygons, butterfly/fish/dragon/world paths with solid, linear and radial fills, SrcOver, 512x600 prgb32 target, shape sizes 8x8 to 256x256, render calls per millisecond, single thread (AGG has no conic or pattern styles in the data: 87 of 174 test rows).
claimed_speedup: Apple M1 Pro, 2026-06-08 run, geometric mean over all test/size cells (derived from page data): 1.21x Skia (faster in 66% of 522 cells; strokes 1.39x, fills 1.08x; only 1.03x at 8x8 and 1.02x at 16x16, 1.39x at 64x64) and 2.29x Cairo (faster in 94% of cells). Intel i9-14900K Windows run (no Skia there): 1.87x Cairo (derived from page data). Slower than Blend2D (0.30x on M1 Pro, derived).
compiler_and_flags: CMake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release per the harness README; compiler and flags not stated in the result data
hardware: Apple M1 Pro (aarch64, macOS); second dataset Intel Core i9-14900K (x86_64, Windows)
stars_or_usage: 367 stars (GitHub mirror of the SourceForge project)
tradeoffs: Header-heavy C++ template library, CPU only, run single-threaded in this harness. Older, lower-level API than Skia or Cairo. The upstream SourceForge AGG 2.4 and this 2.6 mirror are dual licensed under a Modified BSD License or the Anti-Grain Geometry Public License.
caveats: Win is workload dependent: against Skia AGG is roughly at parity for tiny shapes (8x8, 16x16) and loses on large rect fills; against Cairo it wins in nearly all cells. The ghaerr repo README notes the bundled General Polygon Clipper code has separate non-commercial terms, so do not copy that part. Last commit on this mirror is 2023-08-21 (a mirror of the SourceForge project, little recent development). The mirror may differ slightly from the AGG copy bundled in blend2d-apps/3rdparty/agg. Ratios are my own aggregation of the published rcpms (render calls per ms) values.
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): LaurenzV/master-thesis main.pdf (Section 5, Vello CPU vs Blend2D bench harness) and the LaurenzV/vello_chart data files data/arm/2026-06-08.json

name: JUCE software renderer (juce_graphics)
workload: Same bl_bench suite as above (JUCE 8.0.8 through juce::Graphics on a juce::SoftwareImageType image): 29 fill/stroke shape tests x five paint styles (solid, linear, radial, two image-pattern filters; no conic) x six sizes 8x8 to 256x256, SrcOver, 512x600 target, render calls per ms.
claimed_speedup: Apple M1 Pro, 2026-06-08 run, geometric mean over 870 comparable test/size cells (derived from page data): 1.68x Skia (faster in 84% of cells; strokes 2.10x, fills 1.40x; 1.26x at 8x8 up to 2.02x at 64x64 and 128x128) and 2.93x Cairo (faster in 95% of cells). Slower than Blend2D (0.41x, derived from page data). No x86 JUCE run in the published data.
compiler_and_flags: CMake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release per the harness README (JUCE added through JUCE_DIR, JUCE_USE_CURL=0, USE_COREGRAPHICS_RENDERING=0); compiler and flags not stated in the result data
tradeoffs: The renderer is part of the large JUCE application framework (juce_graphics, juce_core, juce_events), not a standalone library; it is single-threaded and CPU only. Dual licensed: AGPLv3 or a paid commercial JUCE licence, so closed-source use needs the commercial licence.
caveats: Single machine for JUCE (M1 Pro); JUCE 8.0.8 was measured while the repo is now at 9.0.3 (2026-09-28); the harness disables JUCE's CoreGraphics rendering (USE_COREGRAPHICS_RENDERING=0) and uses SoftwareImageType, so JUCE's own software renderer ran. Harness is a LaurenzV fork of the Blend2D bl_bench tool (github.com/LaurenzV/blend2d-apps, bl_bench with backend_skia.cpp, backend_juce.cpp, AGG, Cairo backends; CMake Release build). Compiler, compiler version and flags are not stated in the result files, hence tier B not A. The runner is the author of Vello CPU (a competitor), and the harness comes from the Blend2D author; the Skia version is not recorded in the data file. Ratios are my own aggregation of the published render-calls-per-ms values; per-test results vary (JUCE is behind Skia on some small-fill tests).
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): LaurenzV/master-thesis main.pdf Section 5 (Vello CPU vs JUCE, AGG, Skia, Cairo, raqote, tiny-skia on M1 Pro) and the LaurenzV/vello_chart data files

name: raqote
workload: Same bl_bench suite via the LaurenzV/raqote_c C bindings; 29 fill/stroke tests x six paint styles (solid, linear, radial, conic, two image-pattern filters) x six sizes (8x8 to 256x256), SrcOver, 512x600 target, render calls per ms.
claimed_speedup: Apple M1 Pro, 2026-06-08 run, geometric mean over test/size cells (derived from page data): 1.08x Skia (faster in 57% of 1044 cells; fills 1.24x, strokes 0.91x, 0.90x at 256x256) and 1.84x Cairo (faster in 80% of 870 cells; 2.27x on fills). Intel i9-14900K Windows run: only 1.09x Cairo (derived from page data). Slower than Blend2D (0.26x on M1 Pro, derived).
compiler_and_flags: Rust crates built with target-feature=+avx2 on x86, default NEON on ARM (thesis Section 5.2); C++ harness CMake Release; compiler versions not stated
hardware: Apple M1 Pro (aarch64, macOS); second dataset Intel Core i9-14900K (x86_64, Windows)
stars_or_usage: 1.2k stars; used by resvg, Servo, orbtk
tradeoffs: Rust crate (needs the raqote_c bindings or FFI from C++); no explicit SIMD, 4x4 multi-sampled anti-aliasing (lower quality than analytic coverage), single-threaded.
caveats: Only a marginal win over Skia (1.08x overall, losing on strokes and on 256x256 shapes) and a modest one over Cairo; a faster-than-Skia claim holds mainly for small fills. Harness is a LaurenzV fork of the Blend2D bl_bench tool (github.com/LaurenzV/blend2d-apps, bl_bench with backend_skia.cpp, backend_juce.cpp, AGG, Cairo backends; CMake Release build). Compiler, compiler version and flags are not stated in the result files, hence tier B not A. The runner is the author of Vello CPU (a competitor), and the harness comes from the Blend2D author; the Skia version is not recorded in the data file.
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): LaurenzV/master-thesis main.pdf Section 5 and the LaurenzV/vello_chart data files

name: AGG.rs (agg-rust, Rust port of AGG 2.6)
baseline: AGG 2.6 (original C++ library, built with MSVC 19.44)
workload: Render-call time of 11 AGG demo scenes (simple_line, lion_outline, rasterizers2, conv_dash_marker, perspective, image_perspective, image_transforms, image_filters, compositing2, flash_rasterizer, flash_rasterizer2) at 430x340 to 655x520, same scene and size on both sides, output byte-identical to C++; 4 passes x 25 timed iterations after 2 warmups, best-of and median reported.
claimed_speedup: Best-of render time Rust/C++: 0.66x simple_line, 0.73x image_transforms, 0.76x flash_rasterizer2, 0.79x flash_rasterizer, 0.86x lion_outline, 0.87x image_filters (so roughly 1.2x to 1.5x faster, derived from page data); about parity 0.96x to 0.99x on perspective, image_perspective, compositing2; slightly slower on rasterizers2 (1.08x) and conv_dash_marker (1.02x). Medians: 0.56x simple_line to 1.26x rasterizers2.
compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.91.0 (cargo build --release) versus MSVC 19.44.35219.0 (CMake --config Release); explicit optimisation flags not stated
tradeoffs: Pure Rust, zero external dependencies, byte-for-byte AGG 2.6 output, also runs as WebAssembly demos. Not callable from C++ without FFI work. Still a CPU scanline rasterizer with AGG's feature set.
caveats: A port of AGG (so a likely fold into the AGG entry as a duplicate); the baseline AGG is not Skia, Cairo or Blend2D. Mostly parity-level results on an old 2-core laptop CPU, with the project's own note that differences under about 2 ms are at the measurement floor; the Rust side runs in-process while the C++ side is a separate agg-render subprocess (render call only is timed). Project's own benchmark, partial flag information, so tier C.
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): WebSearch for AGG repositories (agg-rust surfaced), then README Benchmarks section and docs/BENCHMARKS.md

name: ctx (2D vector rasterizer and terminal by Oyvind Kolas)
baseline: Cairo (with pixman); Qt6 also compared; Blend2D is faster than ctx in the same tournament
workload: The ctx.graphics 'rasterizer tournament' (Blend2D bl_bench style tests such as FillRectA-256x256-SrcOver-Solid, stroke and gradient tests) comparing ctx, Blend2D, cairo and Qt6.
claimed_speedup: From search-result snippets of ctx.graphics/performance (page itself blocked here): in 8-bit mode ctx is 'comparable to - and often faster than' cairo/pixman; cairo still faster for opaque fills; partially transparent color fills 1.25x faster than cairo/pixman; gradient fills 5x faster than cairo/pixman. Blend2D is faster than both cairo and ctx, in some micro benchmarks almost twice as fast as ctx. One snippet of the scoring table reads Blend2D 259 wins, ctx 61, Qt6 1, cairo 3.
compiler_and_flags: clang; cairo and qt6 from Debian packages; Blend2D linked statically (per snippet)
hardware: AMD Ryzen AI 7 445, core locked at 2.0 GHz (per snippet)
stars_or_usage: 8 stars on this unofficial GitHub mirror (upstream is cloned from ctx.graphics)
tradeoffs: Portable C with auto-vectorization, single header ctx.h, aimed at microcontrollers up to threaded colour-managed float rendering; HTML5-canvas-like API. LGPLv3+ renderer (the ctx terminal is GPLv3+).
caveats: SNIPPET ONLY: ctx.graphics, pippin.gimp.org and the upstream git are blocked in this environment, so the tournament page was never opened and no numbers were checked on a page; one search summary also gave a contradictory total ('1613 heats'), so treat the numbers as unverified. The repo opened is the unofficial GitHub mirror (last commit 2024-10-01, default branch dev); the upstream project is probably more recent. The claim against Cairo is mixed (cairo wins opaque fills) and ctx loses to Blend2D, so a verifier with access to the tournament page should re-check before using. License taken from COPYING on the mirror's dev branch.
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): WebSearch 'ctx.graphics ctx vector graphics terminal microcontroller rasterizer performance tournament Blend2D Cairo AGG Qt github mirror' and a follow-up domain-restricted search

name: Blend2D (vello_chart shootout aggregate)
workload: bl_bench-style suite in LaurenzV/vello_chart: 29 fill/stroke shape tests x six paint styles (solid, linear, radial, conic, two image-pattern filters) x six sizes (8x8 to 256x256), SrcOver, 512x600 prgb32 target, render calls per ms; Blend2D 0.12.0 single-threaded and 2, 4, 8 threads.
claimed_speedup: Apple M1 Pro, 2026-06-08 run, geometric mean over all test/size cells (derived from page data): single thread 4.08x Skia (faster in 99% of 1044 cells; 2.52x at 8x8 rising to 5.61x at 256x256) and 7.11x Cairo (99% of 870 cells); 8 threads 11.45x Skia and 20.55x Cairo (8 threads 2.81x its own single thread). Intel i9-14900K Windows run: 6.13x Cairo (no Skia there).
compiler_and_flags: CMake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release per the harness README; compiler and flags not stated in the result data
hardware: Apple M1 Pro (aarch64, macOS); second dataset Intel Core i9-14900K (x86_64, Windows)
tradeoffs: Uses a JIT (AsmJit) pipeline generator; C++ library with its own text, image codecs and stroker.
caveats: Extra independent-style evidence for the already known Blend2D entry (same thesis data as the papers entry, but aggregated over the full result file). Harness is a LaurenzV fork of the Blend2D bl_bench tool (github.com/LaurenzV/blend2d-apps, with Skia, JUCE, AGG and Cairo backends; CMake Release build); compiler, compiler version and flags are not stated in the result files, hence tier B not A. The runner is the author of Vello CPU and the harness comes from the Blend2D author, so neither is neutral for these two libraries; the Skia version is not recorded in the data. Data used Blend2D 0.12.0 while the repo is at v0.21.3, so current speed may differ.
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): github.com/LaurenzV/vello_chart data/manifest.json and data/arm/2026-06-08.json, linked from the LaurenzV/master-thesis main.pdf

name: Vello CPU (vello_chart shootout aggregate)
workload: Same bl_bench-style suite as the Blend2D aggregate entry (29 tests x six paint styles x six sizes, 512x600 target, render calls per ms) with vello_cpu through the LaurenzV/vello_cpu_c C bindings; single thread and 2, 4, 8 threads.
claimed_speedup: Apple M1 Pro, 2026-06-08 run, geometric mean over all test/size cells (derived from page data): single thread 2.50x Skia (faster in 91% of 1044 cells; 1.59x at 8x8 rising to 3.42x at 256x256) and 4.33x Cairo (94% of 870 cells); 8 threads 7.54x Skia and 12.55x Cairo (3.02x its own single thread). Intel i9-14900K Windows run: 2.75x Cairo. Slower than Blend2D single-threaded (0.61x on M1 Pro, 0.43x on i9, derived).
compiler_and_flags: Rust crates built with target-feature=+avx2 on x86, default NEON on ARM (thesis Section 5.2); C++ harness CMake Release; compiler versions not stated
hardware: Apple M1 Pro (aarch64, macOS); second dataset Intel Core i9-14900K (x86_64, Windows)
stars_or_usage: 4.4k stars (linebender/vello, which also holds the GPU renderer)
tradeoffs: Rust crate (needs the C bindings or Rust FFI from C++); sparse-strips architecture with SIMD and optional multithreading; also has a hybrid CPU/GPU variant.
caveats: Extra evidence for the already known Vello CPU entry. Harness is a LaurenzV fork of the Blend2D bl_bench tool (github.com/LaurenzV/blend2d-apps, with Skia, JUCE, AGG and Cairo backends; CMake Release build); compiler, compiler version and flags are not stated in the result files, hence tier B not A. The runner is the author of Vello CPU and the harness comes from the Blend2D author, so neither is neutral for these two libraries; the Skia version is not recorded in the data. The vello_chart data is run by the Vello CPU author (LaurenzV), who also wrote the thesis, so this is not a neutral third-party measurement for Vello CPU; the repo page now lists vello_cpu as a top-level vello_cpu/ directory (the thesis footnote points to sparse_strips/vello_cpu).
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): github.com/LaurenzV/vello_chart data/arm/2026-06-08.json, linked from the LaurenzV/master-thesis main.pdf
